description: Applying object tags via ALTER <object> SET TAG / UNSET TAG across the applicable object types (database, schema, table, column, view, warehouse), plus ALLOWED_VALUES enforcement and the tag-must-exist requirement - asserted through the SQL surface, SYSTEM$GET_TAG. A view answers under the TABLE domain (the VIEW domain is refused, naming TABLE as the domain for all table-like objects), several tags set in one statement, tag lookup keyed by the canonical upper-cased name, and TAG_REFERENCES is a table FUNCTION on a real account rather than a readable view. Converted 1:1 from features/ObjectTaggingTest (now retired). Each test creates its own tags and objects, and drops the account-level warehouse it made.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
ALTER TABLE t SET TAG cost_center = 'engineering'
ALTER TABLE t UNSET TAG cost_center
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN name SET TAG cost_center = 'pii'
ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN name UNSET TAG cost_center
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT id FROM t
ALTER VIEW v SET TAG cost_center = 'analytics'
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT id FROM t
ALTER VIEW v SET TAG cost_center = 'analytics'
